analysis.title: What's Top of Mind in Macro Research: G10 central banks, some election surprises, AI jitters ebb and flow
key_insights: The Fed held rates at the 10/28 meeting as expected. GS read Chairman Warsh's comments as balanced and consistent with both a slower every-other-meeting hiking pace and a limited total number of hikes.
GS expects a second and final Fed hike in December 2026. A third hike in March 2027 is possible if inflation comes in higher than GS expects, even though GS sees downside risks to growth.
Warsh announced changes to the frequency of policy statement and rate decision meetings starting next year, and announced task forces. GS will keep a close eye on both.

GS expects the ECB to hold at the 10/29 meeting and deliver a final 25bp hike in December. Tighter Euro area financial conditions from turbulence in the French bond market could substitute for tightening and pose downside risk to that forecast.
A further rise in energy prices, particularly gas, could make an ECB hike in March 2027 possible.

GS expects the BoJ to hold at this week's meeting with no substantial changes to the October Outlook report assessments. The next BoJ hike is expected in January 2027, and the press conference is the item to watch for clues.
The BoC hiked 25bp on 10/28. GS expects a hold in December given likely Q4 growth weakness, then a final 25bp hike in January 2027.

Lula's surprise win in Brazil's presidential election triggered a significant repricing across Brazilian assets. The Finance Minister appointment and the fiscal consolidation strategy are the key items for asset performance.
GS expects modest spending-growth containment and further tax increases under a fourth Lula term. With the tax burden already high, GS believes a fiscal regime shift will be difficult to achieve.

Netanyahu's Likud performed better than expected in Israel's election, but no party has a majority, so coalition-building is likely. GS thinks a significant shift in Israel's security and foreign policy is unlikely because the main blocs broadly agree on these issues.

US midterms next week remain the key focus, with prediction markets assigning high odds to a Democratic sweep. GS does not view AI regulation risk or Iran conflict escalation as particularly sensitive to the outcome.
If both AI regulation and Iran escalation materialize after the midterms, GS thinks it could weigh on equities and Treasury yields, with mixed implications for the broad Dollar.

Q3 earnings season is tracking substantially stronger than expected. Over half of reporting S&P 500 companies have beaten consensus EPS, and upgrades to analyst earnings estimates outnumber downgrades.

GS expects S&P 500 earnings growth to decelerate in coming years as the AI investment tailwind fades, so it expects the AI trade to stay volatile. Recent labor data shows some signs of AI-related hiring headwinds, and GS expects questions about AI labor displacement to grow.
China's property downturn is deeper than GS previously anticipated. GS expects the drag on real GDP growth to narrow from 1.8pp in 2026 to 1.3pp in 2027 and largely fade by 2030.
earnings_insights: Q3 2026 S&P 500 earnings season: GS estimates over half of reporting companies have beaten consensus EPS, and estimate upgrades outnumber downgrades.
GS S&P 500 EPS forecasts: $375 for 2026 and $415 for 2027, versus consensus of $367 and $426. GS growth forecasts are 36% for 2026 and 11% for 2027, versus consensus of 34% and 16%.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 earnings are tracking substantially stronger than expected, with over half of reporting S&P 500 companies beating consensus EPS and estimate upgrades outnumbering downgrades.
tension_points.bear_case: The AI investment tailwind gradually fades, so S&P 500 earnings growth decelerates in coming years. Long-term sustainability and returns of AI investment are in question, and AI-related hiring headwinds are showing in labor data.

tension_points.bull_case: Warsh's comments were balanced and consistent with a slower every-other-meeting pace and a limited total number of hikes, ending with a final hike in December.
tension_points.bear_case: Inflation higher than GS expects could bring a third hike in March 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation coming in higher than GS expects would put a third hike in March 2027 in play.

theme_stances.key_argument: The Fed, ECB, BoJ and BoC are mostly holding before delivering further final hikes, with the Fed's second and final hike expected in December.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to expect a second and final hike in December

theme_stances.key_argument: Earnings growth should decelerate as the AI investment boom tailwind fades, keeping the AI trade volatile.
theme_stances.evidence: we think the AI trade will remain volatile

theme_stances.key_argument: AI regulation and Iran escalation are not seen as particularly sensitive to the midterm outcome, but both materializing could weigh on equities and yields.
theme_stances.evidence: we do not view the risks of increased AI regulation
